Recent News

Nov
16
Implementing the Revised Reduction in Force Regulations: Updated Workforce Reshaping Handbook

Washington, DC — Memorandum regarding the updated Workforce Reshaping Handbook, which guides agencies through reshaping actions such as transfer of function and reduction in force (RIF) and reflects the revised RIF regulations, which took effect September 2, 2026.

Nov
16
Modernizing Federal Classification and Qualification Standards Around Skills (Reclassification and Requalification Initiative)

Washington, DC — Memo informs agencies that OPM is moving 600+ occupational series to skills-based standards in 22 cycles starting in FY 2027. For each cycle, agencies must apply the standards to new and reclassified positions within 120 days and finish reviewing existing positions within 365 days.

Nov
16
Issuance of Competency Based Classification Standards for Administrative Occupational Series

Washington, DC — Memo informs agencies that OPM is issuing new standards for eight series in Cycles 1 and 2 (about 220,000 positions). They take effect Monday, March 22, 2027, and agencies must finish reviewing existing positions by Monday, November 29, 2027. The appendix of the memorandum includes answers to frequently asked questions.

Nov
16
Issuance of the Super Intelligence-Assisted Position Review Toolkit

Washington, DC — Memo includes an attached optional, standing Reclassification and Requalification Super Intelligence-Enabled Position Review Toolkit of methodology, prompt sets, and guardrails to help agencies use Super Intelligence (SI) to triage and speed the aforementioned position reviews. Qualified humans must validate all SI output, and agencies must follow privacy rules and keep records.

Nov
10
Final Regulations on Personnel Management in Agencies and Strategic Human Capital Management

Washington, DC — Announces OPM’s final 5 CFR part 250 rule, effective November 30, 2026, and instructs agencies to: 1. Replace Human Capital Operating Plans, Human Capital Reviews, and HRStat with Annual Staffing Plans, Annual Staffing Reviews, and Quarterly Staffing Plan Performance Reviews; 2. Maintain a Strategic Hiring Committee to oversee hiring and ensure hiring aligns with mission needs and the Annual Staffing Plan; 3. At each Annual Staffing Review, have the agency head certify in writing that the CHCO has the access and authority needed for visibility, oversight, and control of the agency's human capital; and 4. Administer their own Annual Employee Survey (AES) using 10 prescribed questions in place of the Federal Employee Viewpoint Survey (FEVS).

OPM Artificial Intelligence

The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) is committed to the secure, ethical, and mission-aligned adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies. In accordance with OMB Memorandum M-25-21, this compliance plan outlines how OPM is building the infrastructure, governance, and workforce needed to responsibly deploy AI across the enterprise. This document reflects our current posture and outlines the steps we’re taking to ensure AI is used to enhance service delivery, protect individual rights, and earn public trust.

Skip to main content

In this section

    Artificial Intelligence Policy

    OPM’s approach is grounded in transparency, accountability, and innovation. We are building a scalable AI ecosystem that supports experimentation while enforcing guardrails that ensure compliance with federal policy and public expectations. This plan is a living document and will evolve as our capabilities mature and as new guidance emerges. 

    • AI Compliance Plan
    • AI Strategy
    • 2026 AI Training

    Artificial Intelligence Inventory

    Executive Order 13960, “Promoting the Use of Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence in the Federal Government,” requires agencies to prepare an inventory of non-classified and non-sensitive current and planned Artificial Intelligence (AI) use cases. Agencies must share their inventories with the public and other agencies to the extent practicable.

    The OPM Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) has created an inventory of OPM AI use cases that satisfies the executive order requirements and increases awareness of AI initiatives. Below, we highlight some AI use cases and provide the complete inventory.
